messages:
sam: FYI we're seeing a 4-6% eviction blip in ap-southeast1 warm pool since 08:02 UTC. Scheduler trace points at failed attach RPCs before preempt churn.
opsbot: [ALERT] region ap-southeast1: warm-pool-evictions > 4% (08:07). Auto-annotate incident.
maria: panel: https://grafana.internal/cluster/ap-southeast1/evictions  spike matches a surge in batch-training pod creations from jobs queue.
linh: do we have kubelet OOM or kube-proxy instability too? Need to narrow to network vs node resource.
sam: logs look like attach/connect timeouts then scheduler tries other nodes and starts preempting. Example: 
```
2026-03-23T08:02:10Z scheduler: bind pod training-42 -> node gpu-aps1-23 failed: attach rpc timeout after 20s
2026-03-23T08:02:11Z scheduler: preempting pod training-41 to satisfy training-42 affinity
```
priyanka: recent infra tuning: we changed fq_codel params on racks B/C to reduce latency tail for small RPCs. Could have increased packet drops under heavy fanout.
jong: TOA: saw qdisc drops and top-of-rack counters spike for two racks. If attach RPCs are getting delayed/dropped, scheduler behavior amplifies it via retries and preempts.
rashid: mitigation options ranked: (1) throttle admissions for batch-training into warm-pool (2) revert qdisc change on suspect racks (3) bump scheduler attach RPC timeout from 20s->45s temporarily (4) relax strict anti-affinity for lower priority jobs. Thoughts?
maria: start least invasive: cap admissions -> drop pod creation rate for training queue by 40% for 30m; concurrently revert qdisc tweak as a canary on racks B/C. If that fixes, we avoid scheduler change.
linh: requesting tc/conntrack dumps from a hot node to validate.
sam: paste from gpu-aps1-23: 
```
# ss -s
TCP: inuse 1187 orphan 0 tw 62 alloc 1187 mem 0
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
12345
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
524288
# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc fq_codel 0: limit 10240p backlog 2300 drops 870 overlimits 1200
```
conntrack not near max but qdisc shows significant drops.
priyanka: that matches hypothesis. I'll roll qdisc revert to previous params on racks B/C as a two-rack canary (2 nodes/rack). jong, can you also add a short admission cap in the batch job controller?
jong: on it 1: admission cap applied to training-queue: max inflight = 30 (was 80). Starting canary now, watching 15m.
opsbot: deploybot: change queued: qdisc-revert-canary -> ap-southeast1-rack-B,C. 2 nodes per rack.
sam: I'll open a scheduler PR to make attach rpc timeout configurable and set default to 45s for canary rollout if needed. Link once created.
priyanka: also spin a staging soak: 250 tiny pods hitting attach path to reproduce. If we still see qdisc drops in staging, revert is less likely to be the fix.
rashid: action items: jong -> apply cap + revert qdisc canary + post runbook link. sam -> scheduler attach-timeout PR. priyanka -> staging soak and metrics collection. linh -> mute noisy alert and set temp threshold to avoid paging. maria -> monitor customer-facing impact and update stakeholders.
maria: thanks. Please post updates in this thread; ping if evictions drop under 1% or if canary fails. :thumbsup:
sam: will post results in ~12m.
__note: Synthetic operational Slack thread for dataset generation. Messages are presented in chronological order and use Slack-style brevity; no title field included per agents.md.
